items.article: First-time homebuyers in expensive US cities are putting FAR more money down than ones in more affordable markets. By BENJAMIN CURRY, US DEPUTY CONSUMER EDITOR For aspiring homeowners, the American dream can now come with a brutal savings timetable: 65 years in New York City , compared with just over three years in parts of Michigan . A new analysis found that a typical household in Warren, Michigan, could save enough for the median first-time buyer down payment in just three years, while Detroit buyers would need nearly four years. At the other extreme, New York City is the toughest major market in America for first-time buyers trying to build a down payment, with a typical household needing more than 65 years to reach a median down payment of $265,000. San Francisco is not far behind, at 57 years for a $400,000 median down payment, while Los Angeles would take 41.5 years to reach its $170,500 median first-time buyer deposit. The huge gap is not simply down to home prices: Buyers in expensive cities are also putting far more money down, with the typical New York first-time buyer putting down 30 percent of the purchase price compared with about 5 percent in Detroit and Warren.

"I was fighting for my life. I realised at that time that if I won't show courage, then 170 passengers will lose their lives," Machchhar told PM Modi during the call. He said that during those difficult moments he was reciting Hanuman Chalisa. "Lord Hanuman gave me courage," he added. He had spoken to the wife and parents of the pilot on Thursday, during which he assured full support from Indian missions for Machchhar and his family. By BENJAMIN CURRY, US DEPUTY CONSUMER EDITOR For aspiring homeowners, the American dream can now come with a brutal savings timetable: 65 years in New York City , compared with just over three years in parts of Michigan . A new analysis found that a typical household in Warren, Michigan, could save enough for the median first-time buyer down payment in just three years, while Detroit buyers would need nearly four years. At the other extreme, New York City is the toughest major market in America for first-time buyers trying to build a down payment, with a typical household needing more than 65 years to reach a median down payment of $265,000. San Francisco is not far behind, at 57 years for a $400,000 median down payment, while Los Angeles would take 41.5 years to reach its $170,500 median first-time buyer deposit.
